test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 15th December 2021 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

There __are still some sugar__ in the bowl.
solution:
The correct option is** "is still some sugar".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Sugar is an uncountable noun so there are no *sugars* or* a sugar* and *are sugar* it goes with** "is still some sugar."**
 
• The nouns that can't be expressed in plural form is called uncountable noun.
 
 
• **Example:** I had a litre of milk today. 
 
 
 
• The correct answer is **"There is still some sugar in the bowl"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• According to the rule of grammar ***is*** is used when the noun is in singular form and ***are ***is used when the noun is in plural form.

 
 
• **Example:**
 
• **Singular:** This is the book I'm eagerly waiting for.
 
• **Plural: **Those Little girls playing in the garden look so happy.
